title: Decrypto
setup: Split players into 2 teams (Team White and Team Black); sit facing each other.
Each team takes their screen, a deck of Code cards, and a note pad.
Draw 4 Keyword cards and slide them into spaces 1, 2, 3, and 4 on your screen (your secret words for the game).
Choose a starting Encryptor for each team (this role rotates clockwise each round).
procedure: Each round plays out in the following steps:
Step 1 - Draw Code Card: Both Encryptors draw 1 secret Code card from their team's deck (e.g., 4 - 2 - 1).

Step 2 - Write 3 Clues: Both Encryptors invent and write down 3 distinct clues corresponding to the 3 secret numbers on their note sheet. Clues must refer to the meaning of the words (no spelling, rhymes, or letters).
Step 3 - Read Clues Aloud: The White Encryptor reads their 3 clues aloud to both teams.
Step 4 - Interception Attempt (Round 2+ onwards): The opposing Black team attempts to guess the 3-digit code based on accumulated clues from previous rounds.
Step 5 - Team Guess: The Encryptor's own White team writes down their guess for the code.

Step 6 - Reveal Code: The White Encryptor reveals the true 3-digit code. If Black guessed correctly, they earn 1 Interception Token. If White guessed incorrectly, they receive 1 Miscommunication Token.
Step 7 - Reverse Roles: Repeat Steps 3 through 6 for the Black team's clues.
endGame: Victory Condition: A team earns 2 Interception Tokens by successfully cracking the opposing team's secret codes.
Defeat Condition: A team receives 2 Miscommunication Tokens due to failed communication within their own team.
Simultaneous End: If both win or lose conditions happen in the same round, calculate final score: +1 point per Interception token, -1 point per Miscommunication token.
⚖️ Tie-Breaker: Each team attempts to guess the other team's 4 secret keywords; most correct keyword guesses wins.
notes: Clue Specificity: Your clues must be clear enough for your teammates to guess the numbers, but obscure enough that opponents cannot decipher the pattern.
Public Information: All written clues remain visible to both teams across all subsequent rounds on their note sheets.
Rotate Encryptor: The Encryptor role MUST rotate each round so every teammate writes clues.
